title: Evening-ease release slate and traffic softening notes (Apr 2026) - WIP
content:
Purpose:
This is a working slate for an ‘evening-ease’ release pattern — target small, low-risk changes that land in lower-traffic evening windows and use traffic softening (gradual ramp down/up, throttles) to avoid user-visible regressions. Primary goal: minimize customer impact while exercising fast patches and small feature rollouts.

Scope and constraints:
- Targeted for features/patches that are backward-compatible at the API level and do not require DB migrations.
- NOT suitable for infra changes that touch central routing, auth, or model-migration flows (those need day-time full-safety windows).
- Default window: 22:00–01:00 PT (check region overlap for APAC customers) — see calendar below.

Quick decision checklist (pre-launch):
- Code: PR green, integration tests passing, performance regression check run (bench + smoke). (owner: PR author)
- Canary: 0.5–1% traffic lane prepared, health checks configured, canary alert thresholds set. (owner: release-engineer)
- Observability: dashboards updated (latency, error-rate, tail-latency), sampling tweaks for traces, low-noise alerts for known signals. (owner: SRE on call)
- Rollback: one-click rollback identified, rollback smoke test defined, post-rollback validation plan drafted. (owner: release lead)
- Communication: standby Slack channel created #release-evening-ease, on-call roster and escalation steps pinned. (owner: release PM)
- Data: confirm no forward-only migrations and no critical schema churn. (owner: data-eng)

Evening rollout calendar (example 3-hour window):
- T-120m: Final code freeze, tagging, and build publish. Confirm artifact checksum.
- T-90m: Canary deploy to 0.5% traffic. Start continuous smoke runner (latency + correctness probes).
- T-60m: Observe 30m of telemetry. If error-rate spike >0.2% absolute or p99 increases >40% relative, abort and rollback.
- T-30m: If canary is stable, expand to 5% with gradual ramp (add 1% every 5 minutes).
- T-0: If stable at 5% for 30m, consider target expansion to 20% (depending on risk profile and capacity). Otherwise hold and follow mitigation play.
- T+60m: Continue monitoring; if no regressions, schedule final expansion next quiet window or follow planned phased rollout.

Throttle and traffic softening heuristics:
- Use soft-throttle curve (traffic weight reductions rather than hard cutoffs) for experimental lanes. Example curve: 100% -> 85% -> 70% over 2 minutes when detecting downstream sluggishness.
- Prefilter heavy/expensive routes to lower-tier pool while canary runs (reduce high-cost queries served by canary to protect capacity).
- Backpressure policy: on sustained p50 latency increase above threshold for 3m, divert 30% of new requests to fallback model variant.

Smoke tests (must be automated and runnable in <5m):
- Basic end-to-end: auth -> request -> response -> correctness assert (small set of golden prompts).
- Latency probe: 50 concurrent short requests measuring p50/p95/p99.
- Cache warmup check: ensure top-10 prefixes cached for common flows to avoid cold-KV storms.

Telemetry guardrails and thresholds (example values — tune per service):
- Error-rate: abort on +0.3% absolute increase over baseline or 3x relative for critical endpoints.
- Tail latency: abort on p99 > baseline*1.6 for 5m window.
- Capacity: GPU mem pressure >85% for 2 consecutive minutes -> throttle rollout expansion.

Rollback matrix (fast):
- Manual rollback: immediate reverse-deploy to previous artifact; notify channel; run rollback smoke tests.
- Automated rollback conditions: if error-rate or p99 crosses threshold AND operator doesn’t acknowledge within 3m, system initiates partial-traffic cut to previous variant.
- Post-rollback: capture quick logs, annotate PR and incident ticket (REL-2026-1123), schedule 24h postmortem if rollback performed.

Communication template (Slack pinned message):
- Title: Evening-ease release — <short feature name> (REL-2026-1123)
- Window: 22:00–01:00 PT; Canary at 22:30
- Owners: Asha Patel (release lead), Marcus Lee (SRE), Sofia Gomez (QA)
- Runbook link: CONFLUENCE: Release windows playbook (internal)
- Rollback contact: oncall@sre.redwood.com (pager duty)

Draft release notes (to send to internal product-watchers / CS if needed):
- Summary: Small server-side optimization to batching kernel selection for v2 models. Expected Benefit: 3–7% token-cost reduction on long-context requests; no API change.
- Risk: Potential p99 latency regressions for underweighted GPUs during cache-warm. Mitigation: soft-throttle and prefix cache warmers in place.
- Rollout plan: Canary -> small expansion -> evaluate telemetry -> expand further in subsequent windows.
- Action for CS: Monitor customer-facing latency tickets; if customers report repeated timeouts, escalate to release channel.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Are there customers in APAC that must be excluded from this window due to daytime business-critical workloads? (action: customer-coverage check, owner: CS)
- Confirm metrics ownership: who tunes the p99 baseline for the new kernel? (owner: perf eng)
- Add a short automation to re-warm prefix cache immediately after deploy (could be a post-deploy Lambda). (owner: infra)
- Decide whether to include dedicated-capacity customers in canary or exclude them by default. (owner: product + sales outreach)

Post-release quick journal template (fill during / after window):
- Canary start time: __
- Canary signals observed: latency=__, errors=__, mem_pressure=__, trace_sample_notes=__
- Decisions taken: expand_to_X% at T=__ because __
- Issues encountered and actions: __
- Final state at T+60: stable / rolled back / held (notes)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep this doc terse — ops need bullet answers in the channel.
- Later: convert stable pattern into a small automation that runs preflight checks and auto-creates the Slack channel + pins runbook.

Related artifacts and references:
- Quick link to perf harness: https://internal.perf/redwood/bench/v2-kernel
- Canary config example (snippet in repo): github.com/redwood-inference/ops/configs/canary-evening.yaml

If you plan to use this window, add a line to the calendar with the PR number and rough blast radius (e.g., "PR#456 - small perf kernel tweak - expected 0.5% initial blast") and ping the release lead 48h prior.

-- Asha (drafted live during on-call handover)
